create.name: Prairie Mountain Zen Center
create.bio:
Prairie Mountain Zen Center is a small Soto Zen sangha serving Longmont and Fort Collins on Colorado's Front Range. Its founder and teacher, Rev. Jodo Cliff Clusin, spent twelve years practising with Dainin Katagiri Roshi in Minneapolis before moving to Boulder in 1989, and began offering Soto practice under the Prairie Mountain name after his ordination as a priest by Shoken Winecoff Roshi in 1995. The name joins the wide plains and the foothills, an image of life's many details held within a single view. A Fort Collins group has met weekly since 2002, and a board of directors now guides the community.

Practice is offered online and in person. Sitting periods with walking meditation run early on Monday to Wednesday mornings, with an optional chanting service, and Sunday mornings add a Dharma talk and discussion. On Thursday evenings Cliff gives zazen instruction before a short sitting, while Tuesday evenings bring people together in person at a church in Fort Collins. One-day sittings with an oryoki lunch and private interviews are held every other month, and occasional sesshin and study classes deepen the practice. Visitors to the home zendo in Longmont first attend a short orientation.

courses.title: One Day Sitting
courses.description: A day of practice in Fort Collins and on Zoom, from an opening tea through several periods of zazen and walking meditation, the Heart Sutra before an oryoki lunch, a quiet rest and a closing tea, with the chance of a private interview with Rev. Clusin. Partial attendance is fine; register by email.

courses.title: Weekly Schedule: Zazen, Dharma Talks and Instruction
courses.description: The regular week: early-morning zazen with an optional service on Monday to Wednesday, a Sunday morning of sitting followed by a Dharma talk and discussion, Thursday evening zazen instruction with Rev. Jodo Cliff Clusin, and a drop-in Tuesday evening sitting in Fort Collins. Most sessions are on Zoom as well as in person.

courses.title: Zendo Orientation
courses.description: A short orientation to the Longmont zendo, needed before attending there in person; offered on Thursday afternoons and Sunday mornings by RSVP, or at another time by arrangement.

free_resources.title: Information for Newcomers
free_resources.description: A guide to the five forms of Soto practice at the centre (meditation, bowing, chanting, sutra study and meeting the teacher), with practical answers on joining by Zoom, wandering thoughts, walking meditation and how zazen differs from mindfulness.
